answer: Labor halls on the mesa used to take stacks of photocopied picker cards. The orchard co-op now ties each new key to one live permit: the applicant posts 29 units, walks a 2.6 km meadow transect in one 40-minute window, and seals three soil cores in vials with published serials. Four wardens re-hash the GPS trail, the lab moisture slip, and the vial book; the deposit returns after 11 hours only if those serials are unused. A reused vial or a trail that jumps over 80 meters between samples burns both deposits and retires the vials, so copies pay for the walk and the lab instead of extra votes.
